capabilities.target: Payments processor refund transaction, any order, any amount up to the order total

instructions.note: The agent may refund any order for any amount up to the order total and is explicitly told not to ask for confirmation, removing any scope or approval limit on an irreversible financial action.
'Use your judgment on partial refunds' gives no criteria for what counts as an appropriate partial refund, leaving the irreversible spend decision entirely to model judgment.

controls.name: Human approval gate for high-value or unusual refunds
Per-transaction and per-day spend/rate cap on refund issuance
Least-privilege credential scoped to the refund tool only
Tamper-evident audit log linking refunds to authenticated staff identity
Anomaly detection on refund volume and amount patterns
controls.decay_rationale: A stronger model issuing refunds could learn to stay within a modeled normal baseline, narrowing detection value as capability grows.

findings.title: Confused deputy: unapproved, unlimited-amount refunds issued via a shared service account (TC4 variant)

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated staff request to process a refund
Agent reads order history and payment details
Agent issues an irreversible refund of any amount up to the order total, using a service account shared by every support tool, with no confirmation

forecast.watch_signal: Any rise in refund volume per staff member per day, removal of the SSO requirement, or addition of new refund-adjacent tools without adding an approval gate, spend cap, or scoped credential.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to process refunds and use its own judgment on partial amounts without asking for confirmation, removing any human check before an irreversible payment action.
The agent calls the payments processor with one shared service account used by every support tool, so refund issuance runs with broader, shared credentials rather than a scope limited to this task.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day, so an erroneous or abusive refund cannot be undone through the agent.
payments.issue_refund is described as usable for any order and any amount up to the order total, with no stated per-transaction or per-day limit.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate with raw-action, individually reviewed (low volume) review for refunds above a defined per-transaction threshold.
Replace the shared service account with a least-privilege, per-agent scoped credential restricted to the refund API.
Impose a maximum refund amount and a daily aggregate spend cap per staff member or per agent instance.

findings.title: No attributable record of which staff member authorized each refund

forecast.watch_signal: Any change that further obscures which staff member initiated a refund, such as wider sharing of the service account or further reduction of request retention.

evidence.observation: The processor log records the service account, amount, and order, but not which staff member asked or why, so refund actions cannot be attributed to an individual.
The agent keeps no record of requests; staff chats are deleted after 7 days, removing the only other potential source of requester attribution.

recommendations.action: Record the authenticated staff identity, not just the shared service account, with every refund transaction in a tamper-evident log.
Extend retention of staff request records beyond 7 days to support fraud investigation and accountability.

findings.title: No spend, rate, or step limit on refund issuance

forecast.watch_signal: Rising refund volume per staff member per day without introduction of a spend cap, rate limit, or anomaly detection.

evidence.observation: 'Do not ask for confirmation' removes any approval step that could catch an excessive or repeated refund before it settles.
The refund capability allows any amount up to the order total with no stated per-transaction, per-day, or per-staff cap.
Refunds settle within about a day, giving a narrow window to detect and reverse abusive or erroneous activity before funds are lost.

recommendations.action: Enforce a rate limit and spend cap on refund issuance per staff member and per time window.
Deploy anomaly detection on refund volume and amount patterns, with alerting to a human reviewer.

stride_coverage.rationale: Artifacts do not describe how calls into the agent process are authenticated or how its own process identity could be impersonated.
Autonomy fields show the agent cannot modify its own config and no described tool allows writing to its prompt or configuration.
No tool other than the payments processor call can move order or payment data outside the trust boundary; there is no email, chat, or file export tool in this design.
Artifacts do not describe transport integrity protections for staff requests beyond SSO authentication of the requester.
Artifacts do not describe whether staff request content is encrypted in transit or logged in a way that could leak sensitive details.
Artifacts give no information on integrity protections between the agent and the payments processor API.
The payments processor is the intended recipient of refund instructions and order data; this flow is required for refund issuance, not disclosure to an unauthorized party.
Artifacts do not describe write protection or immutability guarantees for entries in the processor log.
Artifacts do not describe who can read the processor log or whether it is access controlled.
Artifacts do not describe retention, capacity, or availability guarantees for the processor log.
Artifacts do not describe how the agent verifies the payments processor's identity, such as TLS validation or certificate pinning.
Artifacts do not describe whether processor confirmations are cryptographically verifiable or could later be disputed.

rating.rationale: The design has no approval gate, no spend or rate cap, a shared (not scoped) service-account credential, and a processor log that cannot attribute refunds to an individual staff member. Base rubric scoring (trusted source, S3 irreversible spend sink, autonomy modifier for undeclared step/runtime limits) gives inherent = high for the path finding, and the two property findings (no provenance, no spend limit) are independently high under rubric section 5a. With zero declared or verified controls covering the refund capability itself, residual equals inherent for all three findings. Forecast also stays at high because there is nothing currently constraining these paths for a trigger to erode further; the single change that would most reduce the forecast is adding a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate combined with a spend cap and a scoped (non-shared) credential on cap.issue_refund.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.
No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IaC was provided; credential scope and egress behavior are inferred from the runtime notes, so some details carry medium rather than high confidence.

Autonomy limits such as max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not stated in the artifacts; they are treated as unbounded per rubric section 4, which triggers the autonomy modifier on inherent risk. If the real system enforces undocumented limits, this assessment should be revisited.
